title: Green Beret
build: Ocean disk, 1986 (C64 Preservation Project G64, green_beret[ocean_1986](!).zip, SHA-1 eb688ed6cb3f23072c6e09671c82dd3e92da5558)

tools.node: 22.22.0 (the port, its lockstep tests and test_play.js), Chromium headless through Playwright for the page

accuracy.note: 60 of the 732 hand-written comments and 20 of the 118 a decoder wrote, checked by a fresh agent against the code; 14 others that shared the wrong ones' beliefs were corrected with them
the jump arc, the Prison Camp's and the Harbour's fights, corrected while the How it works and Maps pages were checked against the game
the whole game ported routine by routine and run in lockstep with the game's code; the corrected comments are enemies_offscreen, guards_send, status_draw, helis_launch and hero_walk_map

exclude: runtime: zero page, the game's pointers, the multiplexer's lists and the music driver's voice state (named in the listing)
runtime: the game's variables (named in the listing); only the hi score after them, $03BD-$03BF, is read before the game writes it

the playfield's screen: it loads holding a leftover screen of the game (rows of $20 and $21, a floor of $FB), which the blank picture (picture_draw 3) clears before anything is shown; the multiplexer writes the sprite pointers at $43F8
include: code: cia2_serial_check, which the start-up copies here from $4030
code: the start-up and the copy source of cia2_serial_check, in what becomes the playfield's screen

authored: the RAM under the I/O area, which holds swapped graphics, the texts of stages 2 and 3 and spare animated characters; block_swap, text_draw and anim_chars_restore read and write it with the I/O switched out

regions: the copy-protection check, copied here from $4030
the virtual sprites, the game's variables and the hi score
the title's logo, the intermission's map and a blank screen, packed
play, the four end-of-stage fights, the title and the opening scene
the playfield's character set and the texts
the Bridge's and the Prison Camp's tiles and their colours
the tiles in use and their colours
the map of all four stages
the status line, the captives' picture, the multiplexer and text drawing
the dogs' shapes for the Harbour's fight
the title's character set, shown in the status band
the Harbour's, the Prison Camp's and the Bridge's characters, under the I/O area
Martin Galway's music driver, 13 tunes and 17 effects
score and status routines and block_swap
